articles.title: Taylor Swift Breakup Song Lyrics for Connor Hellebuyck and the Ongoing NHL Trade Dramas
articles.summary: In one of the most galaxy-brained decisions we've seen in recent memory, Connor Hellebuyck was not in net in his first trip to Winnipeg as a New Jersey Devil.
articles.body:
In one of the most galaxy-brained decisions we've seen in recent memory, Connor Hellebuyck was not in net in his first trip to Winnipeg as a New Jersey Devil.

"I can feel the frustration of the fans," Jets head coach Scott Arniel said . "I can feel the frustration just in the fact that we wanted to get this put to bed. That's the biggest thing. Now it's not getting put to bed here. It's going to linger, but it is what it is."

Meanwhile, the Devils maintain that they had their reasons.

"This has been an organizational decision for us that we debated at length," GM Sunny Mehta said in a statement. "Connor Hellebuyck was adamant that he felt a duty to play on Tuesday in Winnipeg. However, in our estimation, playing in this game would potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability."

To be fair, the Devils have a two-game series with the in-division Capitals next on deck. It makes sense that they're focused on winning hockey games and continuing to rack up divisional points against actual playoff contenders in the Metro.

At the same time, it feels like the latest in a series of slaps in the face from Hellebuyck to the Jets fanbase, and the comments from his former teammates indicate disappointment, too.

In honor of all the mess and all the drama, here are the perfect Taylor Swift breakup song lyrics for each ongoing NHL trade request saga.

And remember, NHL fans: Our girl Taylor might have given us these gut-wrenching ballads, but look at her now. Be patient, and feel all of your feels in the meantime.

There was nowhere for me to stay/But I stayed anyway.

The Dylan Larkin saga is pretty heartbreaking all around. The hometown kid spent a decade with his beloved Red Wings and rose to captaincy. He saw hope and promise roll through town with great drafting, as players like Moritz Seider and Lucas Raymond joined the fold.

But the Yzerplan had nearly a decade to unfold, and even though the right in-house pieces kept developing, GM Steve Yzerman failed to keep his thumb on the trade and free-agent markets. You thought his most successful move—acquiring Alex DeBrincat—would've encouraged him to keep making those kinds of moves. Season after season, we were wondering when the final touches would be made, and we were treated to post-prime Patrick Kane and Vladimir Tarasenko.

You can't really blame Larkin for being fed up, especially when management is now stalling on hiring a full-time GM to replace Yzerman.

There was nowhere for Larkin to stay, but he stayed anyway —on the bench, that is.

I've got some regrets, I'll bury them in Florida / Tell me I'm despicable, say it's unforgivable

I think we can all agree that the Brady Tkachuk and the Senators saga has finally come to a close.

He faced the music on Oct. 21 and scored a goal in his return to Ottawa, but the Senators ultimately got their revenge with a 5-1 win and two important in-division standings points.

We probably won't remember the exact score of Tkachuk's first game back in Ottawa, but we will remember each and every way Senators fans called him " despicable " and said it's "unforgivable."

They're bringin' up my history/But you aren't even listening.

It's often hard to stay focused on the task at hand amid contract talks and trade rumors, but Quinn Hughes and the Wild have done a fantastic job of shutting out the noise as they keep strengthening their hold on the Central Division.

Ironically, that feels like the exact thing they need to do to keep a player like pending UFA Hughes in the first place.

Fans and media are constantly speculating on this situation and wondering if he will marry the Wild and extend his contract, then they're " bringing up his history " and wondering if he will opt to join the Devils with his two brothers.

The Wild? They aren't even listening. They're just piling up the wins and giving Hughes a refreshing respite from the constant noise. It just might work.

Nikita Kucherov and the Tampa Bay Lightning

Puttin' someone first only works when you're in their top five.

Of all the trade request drama to emerge this season, Nikita Kucherov's trade request from the Lightning was the most baffling on the surface.

He's not looking for a tax break; the team is in a playoff spot, and Kucherov wasn't part of that Team USA band of brothers at the forefront of most of these requests.

According to him, there's been a lack of communication from management about his looming contract extension.

"Over the last four months, there have only been two conversations and [GM] Julien [BriseBois] made it clear I'm free to walk on July 1," he said. "It was never about the money for me. It was more poor communication and respect."

Reigning Hart Trophy winner Kucherov's impact on this team can't be understated, and if true, the Lightning will regret putting his contract extension talks in the basement .

Zach Werenski and the Columbus Blue Jackets

I'm getting tired even for a phoenix/Always risin' from the ashes.

Are the Blue Jackets losing Zach Werenski ? He has remained with the team this season after trade discussions and rejected a move to the Dallas Stars in the offseason, but what's next?

Those trade discussions and proposals didn't happen in a vacuum—they happened after discussions in which Werenski informed the team that, beyond his contract ending at the end of the 2027-28 season, he " wasn't sure of his future " in Columbus.

He probably intended to prepare the Blue Jackets for a future without him years down the line, but he'd just come off a career season, a Norris Trophy, and an Olympic win. Of course, they were going to try to scour the trade market and see what they could get when his stock was peaking if he wasn't intending to sign a long-term extension.

The Blue Jackets are in the midst of another lost season as Werenski leads the team in assists and time on ice, and he's clearly tired of going to war for this team and rising like a phoenix to no avail.

I didn't have it in myself to go with grace/'Cause when I'd fight, you used to tell me I was brave.

You might just want to listen to the entire track , as it feels eerily reminiscent of Hellebuyck's departure from Winnipeg, especially upon his return Tuesday.

There's been much ado about the netminder not taking the ice on his first trip to Winnipeg as a Devil. It's justified: He spent 11 years with the Jets, putting up some of the best goaltending seasons in NHL history.

The abrupt nature of his trade request and his decision to sit out training camp soured and shattered a decades-long relationship with Jets fans. I'm sure he would agree that he didn't exactly go with grace.

Still, Hellebuyck is probably thinking: "Hey, if I'm dead to you, why the heck are you attending this game (or this wake) in the first place?" He did so much to try to bring a Cup to Winnipeg through all these years, but the combination of the lack of a true Cup-caliber full team around him, and some tough games from him when it counted, amounted to nothing but bitterness all around now that all is said and done.

Clearly, Hellebuyck didn't have it in himself to go with grace and suit up for his first game back. And as much as Jets fans are justifiably aiming for his heart and going for blood, it's all because they still miss him in their bones.

articles.title: Super League expansion: Brian Carney says Super League dancing to Peter V'landys' tune after vote to expand competition
articles.summary: Brian Carney has said that Super League clubs are dancing to the tune of NRL executive chairman Peter V'landys; Carney also discussed thepros and cons of potential inclusion of London Broncos after the vote to expand the league to 15 teams
articles.body:
It is understood that teams will be allowed to apply to fill the Super League's new 15th place , with London Broncos rumoured to be the favourite to take the available spot.

Carney, though, feels this is a move that plays directly into the NRL's hands after a strategic partnership between the two leagues was announced earlier this year:

"If London are admitted, two issues are worth considering," Carney said.

"The first is that this is the power of Peter at work. NRL chief Peter V'landys made London's presence in Super League in 2028 a prerequisite of any strategic partnership. He was absolutely insistent, and he got his way.

"Knowing London were effectively guaranteed a place in 2028 will undoubtedly have influenced the vote to expand, and quite possibly the decision to bring them in a year early.

"The clubs are, to a degree, dancing to his tune."

Is London Broncos' potential inclusion fair?

Carney also questioned whether London Broncos' potential inclusion in the Super League would be fair on other clubs seeking to be involved, with the Plough Lane side 16th in the IMG grading system that ranks the sustainability of rugby league clubs.

"As this process only began after the NRL suggested that London Broncos had to be in to secure their investment, everyone assumes that it will be London that comes up," he said.

"This is despite them being 16th in the IMG gradings, which were introduced to bring a data led process to promotion and relegation.

"We have of course been here before. Last year the Super League was expanded to 14 on the argument that the fans did not want repeat "loop" fixtures [when Super League teams play four of their 27 league fixtures based on who finished in even or odd-numbered positions].

"I opposed the admission of Toulouse and York [in 2025] on a simple principle: if you cannot offer a club full central distribution, you are not ready to admit them. We also saw the dangers of making reduced distribution a condition of entry with Bradford Bulls back in 2013.

"The new process means that clubs will be well within their right to challenge London. Will Barrow, who finished 15th on IMG rankings, be persuaded to submit an application? Do Widnes think they have more to offer than London?"

The former Warrington Wolves player also raised the issue of a suitable venue and matchday experience as a factor that London Broncos have struggled with since their inception in 1980.

"Since the London Broncos' nascence as Fulham RLFC at Craven Cottage in 1980, they have moved from ground to ground across London playing to an ever-dwindling number of fans," Carney added.

"When Super League was born in 1996, they were to be the centrepiece to the game's growth. They signed genuine national superstars in Shaun Edwards and Martin Offiah. They even had Britain's most famous businessman [Richard Branson] as its owner - and even he could not make it work.

"I raised precisely this with [new Broncos co-owner] Grant Wechsel earlier this year. How will they fill stands that have rarely been full? How will they engage an audience that has shown little sustained interest in almost 50 years?

"Blaming ground moves, or an imbalance between spending on the playing squad and investment off the field, misses the point. Those decisions were made because previous approaches weren't working.

"In Wigan, St Helens or Wakefield, the game is woven into the life of the town. It is passed from parent to child and it is part of what it means to belong to the place.

"At the moment, London has no such inheritance to draw on - and no amount of new players will change that.

"London cannot simply copy the heartlands model and expect a different outcome.

"What London does have is the chance to do things radically differently. It's a city of 9 million people who will pay handsomely to be entertained and almost none of them have fixed ideas about how a rugby league club ought to behave. If London Broncos on a Thursday night became a festival with a rugby league match attached, I'd say they were getting somewhere.

"Think of the Savannah Bananas, who took a sport many Americans had stopped watching and turned it into the hottest ticket in the country. They put entertainment first and made every game an experience people actively want to be part of. Rugby League would still be at its heart; it just wouldn't be the only reason to come.

"It is often said about Manchester that they do things differently there. London Broncos should make that line its own. If you always do what you've always done, you'll always get what you've always got.

"This is the London Broncos' moment. It's time to do things differently."

articles.title: El Rayo se entera... por la prensa de la decisión de extinguir la concesión del Estadio de Vallecas
articles.standfirst: La entidad franjirroja todavía no ha recibido ninguna notificación oficial y no puede iniciar las acciones pertinentes. Su postura es firme: mantener la concesión, adquirir el estadio o buscar una alternativa.
articles.summary: La entidad franjirroja todavía no ha recibido ninguna notificación oficial y no puede iniciar las acciones pertinentes. Su postura es firme: mantener la concesión, adquirir el estadio o buscar una alternativa.
articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano conoció a través de los medios de comunicación que la Comisión Jurídica Asesora de la Comunidad de Madrid considera procedente extinguir definitivamente la concesión del Estadio de Vallecas. Una noticia de enorme trascendencia para la entidad franjirroja, que todavía no ha recibido ninguna notificación oficial al respecto y se encuentra a la espera de conocer los términos del dictamen. La situación abre un nuevo capítulo en las diferencias entre el club y el Gobierno regional por la gestión del recinto. El pronunciamiento del órgano consultivo supone un paso importante dentro del procedimiento administrativo, aunque todavía será necesario conocer cómo se materializa y cuáles son sus consecuencias. La ausencia de una comunicación formal impide al Rayo conocer con exactitud los argumentos jurídicos sobre los que se sustenta el procedimiento. Por ese motivo, la entidad no puede pronunciarse públicamente sobre su contenido ni determinar todavía qué actuaciones llevará a cabo para defender sus intereses. Entre las opciones que contempla el club figura la solicitud de medidas cautelares, una herramienta con la que trataría de proteger su posición ante una eventual retirada de la concesión. Sin embargo, cualquier iniciativa dependerá de la documentación que reciba y del análisis que realicen sus servicios jurídicos. La entidad rayista quiere conocer primero el alcance de la resolución antes de establecer su estrategia. Al margen del procedimiento administrativo, en Vallecas han llamado especialmente la atención las declaraciones realizadas el pasado viernes por Mariano de Paco durante la presentación del torneo DiscapRayo. El consejero de Cultura, Turismo y Deporte de la Comunidad de Madrid aseguró que el Rayo seguirá jugando en su actual estadio, una afirmación que sorprendió dentro del club: "El mensaje que quiero transmitir es que el Rayo va a seguir jugando en su campo y será un mejor campo, sin duda alguna", aseguró De Paco. La entidad considera que esa decisión le corresponde exclusivamente a ella, independientemente de lo que determine el Gobierno regional sobre la gestión de las instalaciones. Para el Rayo, una cosa es la titularidad o la concesión del recinto y otra diferente que pueda darse por hecha su continuidad como usuario del estadio. El planteamiento de la entidad es firme: o continúa siendo concesionaria del Estadio de Vallecas, o se convierte en propietaria, o tendrá que buscar alternativas. No contempla como solución definitiva permanecer en el recinto bajo cualquier fórmula de gestión impuesta por terceros. Esta posición introduce una cuestión fundamental en el conflicto: la posible extinción de la concesión no garantiza por sí misma que el Rayo vaya a continuar disputando sus encuentros en Vallecas. El club entiende que necesita controlar las condiciones en las que desarrolla su actividad y no da por asegurada su permanencia sin una solución que responda a sus exigencias. La búsqueda de otra sede, por tanto, es una posibilidad real dentro del planteamiento de la entidad si finalmente pierde la concesión y tampoco puede acceder a la propiedad del estadio.

articles.title: Connor Hellebuyck, Devils Trolled by Jets as Star Sits Out in 1st Winnipeg Trip Since Trade
articles.summary: The Winnipeg Jets took a shot at the New Jersey Devils after the Devils decided against playing former Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck in Winnipeg's 4-2 home win on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The Winnipeg Jets took a shot at the New Jersey Devils after the Devils decided against playing former Jets goalie Connor Hellebuyck in Winnipeg's 4-2 home win on Tuesday.

In a post on X following their victory, the Jets trolled the Devils by writing, "Expected win probability 100%."

That was in response to the Devils posting a statement made by general manager Sunny Mehta on Sunday regarding why Hellebuyck would not face his former team on Tuesday:

In the statement, Mehta said that Hellebuyck against Winnipeg playing would "potentially give us a reduction in our expected win probability."

With Jake Allen getting the start in net over Hellebuyck, the Devils fell behind 2-0 in the first period. They surged back with two goals in the second to tie it, but Winnipeg won it in the third, as Dawson Mercer scored the game-winner, and Kyle Connor added an empty-net goal.

Mercer was fittingly part of the Hellebuyck trade, which was completed last month.

Amid a trade demand, Hellebuyck was suspended by the Jets to start the 2026-27 season, before finally sending him to the Devils for Mercer, Alexander Command, Nick Bjugstad, Nico Daws, a 2029 second-round pick and a 2027 seventh-round pick on Oct. 23.

Hellebuyck had been the face of the franchise and arguably the main reason why the Jets made three straight playoff appearances from 2023 to 2025.

The 33-year-old Hellebuyck was a four-time All-Star, three-time Vezina Trophy winner as the NHL's best goaltender and one-time Hart Trophy winner as NHL MVP during his Jets tenure.

He also led Team USA to its first Olympic gold medal in men's ice hockey since 1980 earlier this year.

Hellebuyck has been excellent since the trade to New Jersey, winning all five of his starts and posting a 1.96 goals-against average and .913 save percentage, but the Devils didn't have the benefit of him being between the pipes in Tuesday's loss.

articles.title: Klatt’s CFP Takeaways: Rankings Committee Is ‘Devaluing The Regular Season’
articles.summary: Joel Klatt reacted to the second slate of College Football Playing rankings, and he's not thrilled about the "SEC feedback loop".
articles.body: Joel Klatt says the College Football Playoff committee is already devaluing the regular season, and he points to its second top 25 as proof. The committee released its second rankings Tuesday night, with Georgia at No. 1, followed by Utah, Alabama and undefeated UCLA. Indiana, the defending national champion, dropped five spots to No. 9 on a bye week. The rankings came a day after the CFP officially announced it will expand to a 24-team playoff beginning in 2027. On the latest episode of "The Joel Klatt Show," Klatt said the rankings show a committee stuck in what he called an "SEC feedback loop." Here are Joel Klatt’s takeaways: 1.Regular Season Is Devalued Klatt’s thoughts: "The big outcry that I hear from fans … is about the devaluing of the regular season, right? That’s what most people will talk about when they talk about their animus toward an expansion to 24 teams. "I would just say — and this is not an argument or a disagreement — but isn’t the committee devaluing the regular season in front of our face? Because it doesn’t matter that Alabama lost two games. UCLA is still behind them, and UCLA is undefeated. So obviously, the regular season is already devalued." 2.Indiana’s Drop Is ‘Wild’ Klatt’s thoughts: "Indiana is 24-1 in their last 25 games, and they are the defending national champions. And they just got bumped five spots in an off week from their couch. That is wild, guys. I totally understand that they have not played a schedule like Texas has played, or Ohio State has played or even Alabama has played. I’m fully aware of that. I understand that they don’t have the marquee win. "But can you imagine a world where, even in the old days, when the SEC was playing their eight conference games and their four non-conference games and a cupcake week in November, you can imagine an SEC defending national champion being 24-1 in their last 25 games and being knocked down five spots in an off week by the College Football Playoff committee? No, you can’t. You can’t imagine that because it would never happen, and yet it just happened to Indiana." 3.1-Loss Teams Are In Trouble Klatt’s thoughts: "Obviously, Indiana, Texas Tech, Wake Forest, they’re the ones being hurt by this feedback loop the most. All three of those teams only have one loss, and yet they’re kind of up against it. "I think Indiana has to get to the Big Ten championship game. If they lose to USC this weekend, there’s a good chance that they’re going to be out of the playoff unless they can somehow get to Indianapolis, and then there’ll be, I would think from the committee some acknowledgement that if you get to the Big Ten championship game, you should be in the College Football Playoff. It is the conference that has won the last three national championships, including Indiana." 4.Big 12 Could Get 3 Bids Klatt’s thoughts: "I do think that the Big 12 is fascinating, though, because BYU is holding strong. Remember, big wins, strength of schedule. They beat Notre Dame. Notre Dame’s in the top five. So BYU is still sitting there, and even if they don’t get to the Big 12 championship game — if Texas Tech were to beat Oklahoma State this weekend and get themselves to Dallas and play Utah, there’s a good chance that those two teams will be playing in the championship game, and BYU would be sitting at home, and I think BYU would be in at that point. "You’re looking at a scenario where maybe the Big 12 could sneak three teams into the College Football Playoff. I think that would be pretty cool. And don’t tell the committee that, though, because they’ll look at that and be like, ‘Hold on, hold on, engage feedback loop. Here we go.’" 5.The 'SEC Feedback Loop' Klatt’s thoughts: "We’re already going down a trajectory where everybody that has influence, in particular around the SEC, pounded the table for strength of schedule, quality wins, the feedback loop. Here we go, and that’s what we’re getting. But other conferences don’t get the benefit of the doubt at all. "We are in a world where the regular season is already being devalued by the committee actively in this poll. There’s no other way around it. They’re in an SEC feedback loop, and we’re likely headed to five SEC teams in the playoff, maybe even six. "Listen, I think it’s still going to be a great playoff. I’m not suggesting that they don’t have great teams and they’re not playing great football, but that’s what the committee is giving us right now, and we’ll see how it plays out." articles.title: New Matvei Michkov Trade Rumors Reveal Star's Stance on Flyers Exit amid Conflicting Reports
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Flyers are reportedly pushing back against rumors that forward Matvei Michkov is interested in a trade.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Flyers are reportedly pushing back against rumors that forward Matvei Michkov is interested in a trade.

The Athletic's Kevin Kurz reported Wednesday a team source said Michkov has not formally requested a trade from the Flyers.

The same source also "strongly denied" Tuesday's report from ESPN's Kevin Weekes that Michkov "would likely want a new start elsewhere," according to Kurz.

General manager Daniel Briere told TSN's Frank Seravalli Michkov's reported desire to leave Philadelphia was "all news to me."

"No, that's not the plan at all. We've never discussed that," Briere said about a potential trade of Michkov, per Seravalli.

Briere continued, per Seravalli: "I've been really happy with how he's played this year... He's been placed in a position to succeed. More minutes, more opportunities, more situations than last year. Matvei is developing. He's far from a finished product."

Michkov, who leads the Flyers with 10 goals in 20 games, is currently set to hit restricted free agency after this season. Kurz noted there is "no guarantee" Michkov will remain in Philadelphia after his current deal expires.

ESPN's Emily Kaplan reported Tuesday the Flyers have "no intention of trading" Michkov, but noted "sources said there has been turmoil behind the scenes between Michkov and the Flyers."

The reports came after Michkov and veteran Flyers defenseman Nick Seeler appeared to have a heated mid-game exchange earlier this week.

Michkov, the No. 7 pick of the 2023 draft, made the jump from the KHL to NHL in 2024 and scored 26 goals as a rookie.

His relationship with the organization came under scrutiny after Rick Tocchet was hired as head coach ahead of his sophomore season.

Michkov's playing time and role fluctuated under Tocchet, who later accused Michkov of arriving to training camp out of shape and made him a healthy scratch during the playoffs.

Tocchet said in September he felt the concern about his relationship with Michkov had been "overblown" but expressed regret about his public remark on Michkov's conditioning, per Kurz .

If Michkov does ultimately push to leave Philadelphia, it wouldn't be the first time the Flyers have dealt with a surprise split between the organization and one of its top players.

The Flyers traded former top-five draft pick Cutter Gauthier to the Anaheim Ducks in January 2024 following what Briere said at the time was Gauthier's unexplained desire not to play for the franchise.

Briere could be hoping the organization is able to maintain a better relationship with Michkov as the Flyers look to bounce back from a 5-10-5 start to the 2026-27 season. Given his expiring contract, however, Michkov will remain a player to watch ahead of the March 2027 trade deadline.

articles.title: Giants Reportedly Pursued Trade For Falcons Superstar RB Bijan Robinson
articles.summary: The New York Giants reportedly contacted the Atlanta Falcons about acquiring superstar RB Bijan Robinson before the 2026 NFL trade deadline.
articles.body: This would've been something! Among other trades they pursued, the New York Giants contacted the Atlanta Falcons about acquiring superstar running back Bijan Robinson before the 2026 NFL trade deadline, according to ESPN. New York was among the most mentioned teams to acquire Indianapolis Colts running back and three-time Pro Bowler Jonathan Taylor. In fact, FOX Sports NFL Insider Jay Glazer reported on Nov. 8 that the Giants offered the Colts a second and fifth-round pick for Taylor. With that said, New York later took the aforementioned trade offer off the table, with Taylor ultimately not being moved by the Colts, who dealt guard Quenton Nelson, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and wide receivers Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, though. The Giants' pursuit of a star back came in the wake of running backs Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy Jr. each suffering hamstring injuries in the team's Week 7 win over the Houston Texans. Granted, Skattebo is expected to return for the Giants' Thursday night matchup against the Washington Commanders, while Tracy could return to action in December. As for the blockbuster trade the Giants inquired about, Robinson, a 2025 All-Pro and a Pro Bowler in each of the last two complete seasons, has an argument for being the best running back in the sport. Through Atlanta's nine games this season, Robinson has rushed for an NFL-high 880 yards and five touchdowns on a career-high 5.2 yards per carry. He has also added 31 receptions for 250 receiving and one score. Atlanta signed Robinson to a three-year, $66.75 million extension in August, with his $22.25 million average annual value second among NFL running backs. While the Falcons are 3-6, they're just a half-game out of first place in the NFC South. In all, New York's offense is 14th in the NFL in total yards (333.1 per game), 16th in both passing yards (221.0 per game) and points (22.8 per game) and 17th in rushing yards (112.1 per game). The Giants stand atop the NFC East at 5-2-1.

Also, the hugely popular one-on-one tournament is returning this coming season in Miami with the first round on Feb. 18, second round and quarterfinals on Feb. 19, and semifinals and finals on Feb. 20.

Many of the biggest stars in women's basketball are set to play, including Collier, Paige Bueckers, Olivia Miles, Breanna Stewart and reigning 2026 WNBA Finals MVP Gabby Williams, who is new to Unrivaled in 2027.

Mist BC are the team to beat entering the season, as Stewart led them to a championship over Phantom BC last season and won Unrivaled Finals MVP honors in the process.

articles.title: Robert Sánchez sale ileso de un accidente tras estrellar un Ferrari en Nürburgring
articles.standfirst: El meta pilotaba un Ferrari 488 Challenge Evo de carreras, valorado en unos 350.000 euros, que quedó destrozado tras impactar contra el guardarrail
articles.summary: El meta pilotaba un Ferrari 488 Challenge Evo de carreras, valorado en unos 350.000 euros, que quedó destrozado tras impactar contra el guardarrail
articles.body: El guardameta español del Como de Cesc Fábregas, Robert Sánchez, se ha llevado un buen susto cuando disfrutaba de un track day con su Ferrari de competición en el Circuito de Nürburgring Nordschleife, que hizo honor a su apodo de 'Infierno Verde'. Según publica el tabloide británico The Sun, el portero internacional propiedad del Chelsea que este año defiende los colores del Como italiano, sufrió un fuerte accidente cuando transitaba con su Ferrari 488 Challenge Evo (un coche exclusivamente de circuitos con 670 CV de potencia) por el punto más icónico del trazado alemán, la curva peraltada del Karussell. Según pilotos conocedores del circuito consultados por MARCA esa zona, pese a no se de altísima velocidad, es especialmente delicada con coches como el Ferrari, tanto a la entrada como a la salida de la curva, "donde es fácil perder el control". Además, los testigos citados por el medio inglés, Sánchez se salió de la pista a una velocidad superior a los 110 km/h impactando contra el guardarail. Las imágenes del Ferrari remolcado por la grúa dan idea de la violencia del impacto, aunque afortunadamente el guardameta no sufrió ningún daño físico. No sucedió lo mismo con el deportivo italiano, que quedó completamente destrozado en su parte delantera... ni con las instalaciones de la pista, que sufrieron daños importantes. Como es lógico, las tandas abiertas que se estaban celebrando en la mañana del lunes, cuando sucedió todo, quedaron neutralizadas mientras los equipos de mantenimiento de la pista limpiaban el trazado y reparaban las protecciones. The Sun cita a testigos del accidente, que describen así lo sucedido: "Se estrelló contra la barrera a unas 70 mph [113 km/h, aproximadamente] y enseguida sacaron la bandera roja en el circuito. Es una curva peraltada con un giro de más de 180 grados y, claramente, aceleró demasiado y se fue directamente contra la barrera. La parte delantera de su Ferrari quedó completamente destrozada y había piezas esparcidas por toda la pista", relatan. Otro participante que pasó por la zona accidentada asegura que el meta "se bajó inmediatamente del coche como si no hubiera pasado nada y empezó a recoger las piezas rotas. No parecía conmocionado ni nada parecido. Solo nos dimos cuenta de que era él cuando vimos que llevaba su nombre escrito en el lateral del coche". Robert Sánchez es un gran aficionado a los coches deportivos... y a la velocidad. Algo que le ha costado algún que otro disgusto en el pasado en forma de multa de radar. En este caso concreto, siempre según la información de The Sun, estaba disfrutando de su pasión por la conducción deportiva dentro de un evento privado organizado por Circuit Days, en el que el número de participantes es más restringido que en las habituales jornadas de puertas abiertas. Eso sí, el accidente le va a costar un 'pico' al futbolista, ya que tendrá que hacer frente a los costes de los daños: tanto en lo que se refiere a los propios materiales (por ejemplo, los guardarraíles) como en el tiempo de trabajo de los marshalls, la grúa o la compensación al circuito por el tiempo en el que la pista no ha estado disponible para el resto de participantes.

articles.title: Polonia tampoco quiere a deportistas rusos compitiendo en su país y niega el visado a los saltadores de esquí
articles.standfirst: Iban a participar en las competiciones de la Copa del Mundo que se disputarán en Wisla y Zakopane
articles.summary: Iban a participar en las competiciones de la Copa del Mundo que se disputarán en Wisla y Zakopane
articles.body: Vladímir Putin se ha topado con otra chinita en el zapato con la que quizás no contaba tras el progresivo levantamiento de las sanciones que pesaban sobre el deporte ruso desde la invasión de Ucrania. Y es que empiezan a ser numerosos los países que se niegan a jugar contra selecciones rusas o directamente deniegan los visados a sus deportistas para que puedan competir en su territorio. En el primer caso hablamos sobre todo del hockey hielo, una disciplina de enorme arraigo en Rusia. El pasado 30 de octubre, el Tribunal de Arbitraje Deportivo (TAS) ordenó a la Federación Internacional de Hockey Hielo (IIHF) admitir a las selecciones nacionales rusas en sus torneos de 2026-27, revocando la exclusión vigente desde 2022. Tres días después, la federación finlandesa, defensora del título, anunció que su selección se negaba a jugar contra Rusia en el Mundial masculino previsto para mayo de 2027 en Alemania. Con todo, el tsunami vino después, porque Suecia, Dinamarca, Noruega, Letonia, República Checa, Austria y Canadá también anunciaron que se sumaban al boicot contra Rusia. Eso era ya la mitad exacta de los 16 países participantes. A todo ello, además, se sumaba la posible retirada de importantes patrocinadores descontentos con el regreso de Rusia. El escándalo estallaba sólo dos semanas después de que Países Bajos denegara el visado a tres gimnastas rusas para el Mundial de Rotterdam, entre ellas la campeona mundial y europea del concurso completo, Anguelina Melnikova. Rusia protestó airadamente y pidió el amparo de la Federación Internacional pero ésta alegó que era un asunto interno que correspondía exclusivamente al gobierno neerlandés. Ahora es el Ministerio de Exteriores polaco el que ha decidido negar los visados a los saltadores de esquí rusos que querían participar en las competiciones de la Copa del Mundo que se disputarán en Wisla y Zakopane, según informó el portal Interia Sport, que cita fuentes de la diplomacia polaca. "De conformidad con el apartado 1 del artículo 3 del Reglamento del Ministerio del Interior y Administración del 13 de marzo de 2020 sobre la suspensión o restricción temporal del tráfico fronterizo en determinados puntos de cruce fronterizo, los ciudadanos de la Federación de Rusia no tienen derecho a cruzar la frontera estatal polaca, que es la frontera exterior de la Unión Europea", señala una declaración de ese Ministerio publicada por Interia Sport. Aunque el reglamento prevé excepciones, "estas no incluyen a los deportistas que participan en eventos deportivos en Polonia", añade. "Por consiguiente, no existen motivos para expedir visados a saltadores de esquí rusos", subraya. La Copa del Mundo de saltos de esquí comienza el 21 de noviembre en Lillehammer (Noruega) y su tercera cita, prevista para el 5 y 6 de diciembre, es ya en Wisla. La de Zakopane, por su parte, será a mediados de enero. Los saltadores rusos no compiten en la Copa del Mundo desde la invasión de Ucrania aunque el TAS falló a su favor en diciembre de 2025 permitiendo que volvieran a competir como neutrales. Pese a ello, no ha sido hasta la nueva temporada cuando saltadores como Danil Sadreev y Evgenii Klimov han regresado al circuito. El pasado verano, el Comité Olímpico Internacional recomendó a las federaciones deportivas mundiales que readmitieran a los deportistas rusos, suspendidos desde el inicio de la guerra en Ucrania. La Federación Internacional de Esquí (FIS) siguió la recomendación del COI y anunció que los saltadores de esquí rusos podrían regresar a la competición bajo bandera neutral, con la condición de no tener vínculos políticos ni militares ni apoyar la guerra de Ucrania. La FIS, sin embargo, también enfatizó que cada país que organice competiciones de la Copa del Mundo decidirá individualmente si permite que los deportistas rusos ingresen a su territorio.

articles.title: Israeli army kills Palestinian footballer Mahmoud Kamal Abdel-Malek in Gaza
articles.summary: Abdel-Malek, the captain and goalkeeper of Gaza Sports Club, recently played in the Thousand Martyrs Cup final.
articles.body:
Palestinian footballer Mahmoud Kamal Fares Abdel-Malek has been killed in an Israeli air strike on Gaza, the Palestinian Football Association (PFA) has confirmed.

The PFA said Abdel-Malek, the captain and goalkeeper of Gaza Sports Club, was targeted in Tuesday’s attack on Gaza City’s southern Sabra neighbourhood.

The 20-year-old was the 1,017th person involved in sport to be killed in Gaza in Israel’s genocidal war on the enclave, according to figures provided by the PFA.

Abdel-Malek’s death came five days after he played in the final of the Gaza and Northern Gaza division of the Thousand Martyrs Cup , a tournament named after the more than 1,000 athletes and sports officials killed in the Strip since October 2023.

“Club legend and goalkeeper of the first team Mahmoud Kamal Fares Abdel-Malik was martyred moments ago,” the club wrote in a social media post announcing his death.

Gaza Sports Club finished as runners-up in the final of the tournament that Al Jazeera covered last week .

More than 200 clubs competed, including 146 from the occupied West Bank, 44 from Gaza, and 36 from Palestinian refugee camps in Lebanon.

The tournament kicked off simultaneously in the three locations.

PFA President Jibril Rajoub said the event showed that Palestinians had not lost their “national will”.

“Nor have we lost our belief that sport will remain a symbol of hope and life,” he added.

Abdel-Malek’s death comes days after Israeli forces killed 15-year-old Mohammad Nidal Barbak on Friday, shooting him while he was playing football with his friends in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis.

The incident has highlighted FIFA’s inaction towards Israel, despite its multiple breaches of the global football body’s anti-discrimination rules.

In March, the PFA called for the Israeli Football Association (IFA) to receive a ban after a report by FIFA’s disciplinary committee found that the IFA “failed to take meaningful action against Beitar Jerusalem” for “persistent and well-documented racist behaviour”.

“We maintain our right and continue our efforts to ensure that the Israeli Football Association is expelled from all international institutions,” Rajoub, who also heads the Palestine Olympic Committee, said at the time.

On the alleged criminal activity of Israeli sports officials, Rajoub said he was referring to instances of players killed during the three years of genocide in Gaza, and the destruction of many of the territory’s sports facilities.

Israeli attacks have devastated Gaza’s sports infrastructure, destroying stadiums, clubs, sports halls and academies as well as bulldozing several sports facilities, Palestinian sports officials say.

The human losses and destruction have left Palestinian sport in an “existential” crisis, according to Palestinian Sports Media Federation Secretary-General Mustafa Siam.

Israel has destroyed more than 50 of Gaza’s 56 sports clubs and about 20 five-a-side football fields established by the PFA with support from FIFA, he told the Anadolu news agency in August.

At least 74,645 Palestinians have been killed since October 7, 2023, while 175,978 have been injured, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health.

articles.title: Nebraska women's basketball gets blowout win over North Carolina A&T
articles.summary: Nebraska closed out its three-game home opener against North Carolina A&T. The Huskers grabbed another blowout win, handling the Aggies, 76-35.
articles.body:
No. 25 Nebraska women's basketball (3-0) closed out its three-game home opener on Tuesday night against North Carolina A&T (1-2). The Huskers grabbed another blowout win, handling the Aggies, 76-35.

Britt Prince took control from the start, hitting three straight shots from beyond the arc in the first quarter. She finished the night delivering a game-high 24 points, shooting 9-of-15 from the floor, 4-of-9 from three-point range and 2-of-3 from the free-throw line. She also snatched three steals.

Her first-quarter surge helped Nebraska go up 20-6, and the lead continued to balloon throughout the night. Meanwhile, North Carolina A&T didn't score 10 points in a single quarter until the fourth. This is the second straight game the Huskers achieved that.

Nebraska shot 29-of-51 on the night, toppling the Aggies offensively by 15 made shots. The Huskers also outshot North Carolina A&T from beyond the arc (7-1). Nebraska outrebounded the Aggies (41-18). North Carolina A&T, meanwhile, shot 14-of-45, 10-of-11 and 6-of-16, respectively.

Amiah Hargrove earned a double-double in the win, scoring 13 points and picking up 10 rebounds. She hit 6-of-8 from the floor and 1-of-3 from three-point range. Ashlyn Koupal also finished in double digits, scoring 11 points on 4-of-8 shooting and going 3-of-3 from the line. She also picked up eight rebounds.

The Huskers head up to Sioux Falls, South Dakota, for a neutral-site clash with Kansas on Saturday in the Marketbeat Invitational. Tipoff is set for 3:30 p.m. CT on B1G+.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Ramifications of Rams Hoping for Puka Nacua to Return Later in the Season
articles.summary: Our latest fantasy football injury update for Puka Nacua discusses how his lengthy absence affects Matthew Stafford and the Rams pass-catchers.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams have placed Puka Nacua on injured reserve, making Sean McVay's squad extremely shorthanded on offense entering Week 10. Ahead of Los Angeles facing the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday, reports have revealed that the Rams are hoping Nacua can return in Week 14 or 15.

With Nacua, Davante Adams, and Terrance Ferguson sidelined for the Rams, there are certainly opportunities available to the remaining skill players.

How does Nacua's injury update affect Matthew Stafford and the Rams' pass-catchers from a fantasy football perspective?

All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. Fantasy rankings and fantasy point totals are courtesy of FantasyPros .

After winning NFL MVP and producing as the QB2 in fantasy points per game (21.1) last season, Stafford is currently the QB16 in fantasy points per game (16.9). Stafford has experienced a slight decline in his production compared to 2025, producing the 13th-most adjusted EPA/play (0.12) and the 17th-highest completion percentage over expected (+0.0%) among the 29 QBs with 200-plus plays in 2026.

While Stafford has already been a risky option with Nacua and his other weapons, he's now unplayable in fantasy given the Rams' current options.

Nacua managers are in a difficult spot after getting consistent WR1 production from the All-Pro wideout whenever he's been healthy. However, while the Rams are hoping for Nacua to return in Week 14 or 15, there's a chance he's not fully healthy before the end of the regular season.

Managers should use an IR spot on Nacua if their league has them, or they should keep him on their bench in hopes he can return for the fantasy playoffs. But if the Rams provide a negative update on Nacua in the coming weeks, he could be worth dropping in favor of someone else who can help in the final weeks.

Of the remaining pass-catchers on the Rams, Tyler Higbee may have the best chance to produce - at least in the short term. Although Higbee is the TE29 in fantasy points per game (6.5), his usage and playing time are positives for an offense that is desperate for receiving production.

In three of the last four weeks, Higbee has logged an 80.0% snap share or higher in a Rams offense that deploys plenty of 12 personnel and 13 personnel looks. Additionally, the Cardinals are permitting the seventh-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to TEs (+3.1).

With a lack of reliable pass-catchers, the Rams could certainly lean on Kyren Williams and Blake Corum more. That being said, someone has to catch passes from Stafford.

Along with Higbee, Tutu Atwell and rookie CJ Daniels are the two deep sleepers to watch in Week 10. That's to say that neither of them is worth starting in any fantasy format against the Cardinals.

None of the other WRs or TEs are currently fantasy-viable, but that could change if a player emerges in Sunday's contest.

articles.title: Phoenix's bench buries Clippers as the same old problem shows up again
articles.summary: The Phoenix Suns got 81 points from their reserves and made a season-high 22 3-pointers in a 133-110 rout of the Clippers on Tuesday night, handing Los Angel...
articles.body:
Whatever good feeling the Clippers carried out of Sunday's win over New Orleans was gone by the end of the first quarter in Phoenix, where the Suns closed the period on a 13-0 run and cruised to a 133-110 win at Mortgage Matchup Center.

Phoenix made 22 of 43 attempts from 3-point range, a season high, and got 81 points from a bench that had five players finish in double figures. The Clippers fell to 2-8 overall and 0-5 on the road, with eight losses in their last nine games.

Jordan Goodwin did most of the early damage in his first game back from a calf injury, making six of his seven 3-point tries for 18 points in 14 minutes. Devin Booker added 17 points and five assists for a Suns team that lost by 26 to San Antonio the night before.

The Clippers held a brief lead late in the first quarter, going up 18-16 before the Phoenix second unit took the game over with the 13-0 run that ended the period.

Goodwin had 15 points by halftime, Luke Kennard hit a pair of 3-pointers off the bench and Collin Gillespie hit a 39-footer at the buzzer that sent Phoenix to the locker room up 64-47. The Suns made 11 of their 22 attempts from deep in the first half, a pace the Clippers had no answer for on either end.

The third quarter went even worse for Los Angeles, with the Suns stretching the lead to 91-59 and taking a 99-72 edge into the fourth. Phoenix sat all five starters for the final period, so the 38-34 fourth quarter the Clippers won against an all-reserve group did little beyond trimming the final margin.

Nov 10, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Clippers guard Darius Garland (10) passes the ball against Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker (15) in the second half at Mortgage Matchup Center.

Darius Garland finished with 13 points, six assists and five rebounds, though he shot 5-of-12 from the field and turned it over four times two nights after his 24-point, 10-assist game against the Pelicans. Rui Hachimura also scored 13 points and made three of his five 3-point attempts.

Rookie Baba Miller scored 13 points off the bench, Max Strus added 12, Derrick Jones Jr. and Keaton Wagler each had 11 and Gradey Dick chipped in 10, giving the Clippers seven players in double figures on a night when none of them could slow Phoenix down, while Kobe Sanders handed out seven assists as a reserve.

The Clippers shot 42 percent from the field and made just one of their 11 shots from midrange, while the Suns piled up 24 second-chance points to 15 for Los Angeles.

I came into Tuesday thinking Sunday's win could be a starting point, since the Clippers moved the ball well against New Orleans and finally looked like a group that trusted each other on offense.

This game showed how thin the margin is for this roster right now, because a road trip to face a Suns team coming off a blowout loss turned into a blowout of its own before halftime.

Injuries explain a good chunk of the slide, with Bradley Beal out with a right knee injury, Brandon Ingram still sidelined with a heel problem and Jordan Miller and Yanic Konan Niederhäuser also out, which leaves Ty Lue leaning on young guards like Wagler and Sanders and a rookie like Baba Miller for real minutes.

Lue said before Sunday's game that Ingram is getting close to a return, and a scorer of his level would take a lot of pressure off Garland and the young guards around him.

Defense worries me even more than the injuries, because Phoenix shot 51 percent from three and 56 percent overall against them, and a team with this little room for error on offense can't hand an opponent 22 3-pointers and expect to win on the road, where the Clippers still haven't won this season.

The schedule doesn't offer much relief either, with the Clippers returning home to host the Oklahoma City Thunder in an NBA Cup game on Friday at 7:30 p.m. at Intuit Dome.

articles.summary: Vote from four nominees for this past week's play of the week: Jeramani Denton (STM), Colin Gardner (Case), Kevin Gomez (CRJ) and Alex Restivo (SH).
articles.body:
What was the best play in Milwaukee-area high school sports last week? You tell us.

This past week featured two plays from playoff football action and two sensational goals on the pitch during the WIAA state soccer tournament and you can decide the best play of the past week by voting from now until noon Saturday, Nov. 14, as many times as you'd like.

We have a submission tool on our Preps Plus portion of the Journal Sentinel website. The location to upload your clips is under the top banner that's labeled " Upload Your Video. " It's a four-step process that will allow you to upload clips from the week across all fall sports. The clips must be trimmed and uploaded to be 30 seconds or shorter in the proper formatting to be eligible for selection. Please submit your clips by the end of the day on Mondays each week to make sure your clip is potentially included to be a nominee.

We also have a step-to-step explainer , along with a link to the Journal Sentinel site, that explains how to upload your own highlight clips for nomination.

If you have any questions about submitting a play of the week nominee, contact Michael Whitlow via email at mwhitlow@gannett.com.

Wauwatosa East vs Whitefish Bay in WIAA Division 2 boys state soccer championship

Jeramani Denton, Saint Thomas More boys soccer

The junior forward scored one of the best goals of the WIAA boys soccer state tournament in the Division 3 state title match Saturday, Nov. 7. With the Cavaliers holding a 1-0 lead late in the first half of STM's 3-1 win over Edgerton , Denton fired a frozen rope of a right-footed strike into the upper 90 at the 35:56 mark to give STM a 2-0 lead on his 15th goal of the season.

Colin Gardner, sr., Racine Case football

Playing in the Division 1 state quarterfinal round for the first time in program history, Gardner drained the biggest kick in Racine Case lore with a walkoff 28-yard field goal as time expired to give the Eagles an improbable 6-3 victory over top-seeded Muskego on the road Friday, Nov. 6, to send Case to the state semifinals.

Kevin Gomez, sr., Cristo Rey Jesuit boys soccer

For the second time in program history in just its 11th year as a WIAA-certified high school, the Cristo Rey Jesuit Trailblazers won the D4 state title with a 2-1 victory over Lake Country Lutheran on Saturday, Nov. 7. The senior forward scored a wonderful goal in the final couple minutes of the first half, chipping the goaltender with a shot attempt a mile high through traffic that gave CRJ a 1-0 lead right before the halftime break for his 33rd goal of the campaign.

Alex Restivo, sr., Sussex Hamilton football

For the third time since 2022, Sussex Hamilton football is on the doorstep of playing for a Division 1 state title. The Chargers advanced to the state semifinal round with a 17-10 victory over defending state champion Arrowhead on the back of an outstanding go-ahead touchdown catch from Alex Restivo in the fourth quarter. The star senior made an amazing diving effort to haul in a Cole Erdmann pass late in the fourth that put Hamilton up for good.

articles.title: Family tradition coming to a close for Bohl family
articles.summary: Nov. 11—MEDINA, N.D. — Things have been a bit crazy between the months of August to November in the Bohl household for the last 13 years. "When I think back...
articles.body:
Nov. 11—MEDINA, N.D. — Things have been a bit crazy between the months of August to November in the Bohl household for the last 13 years.

"When I think back on volleyball seasons growing up, I remember how busy and chaotic our house could get, but also how much fun it was," said Gracie (Bohl) Fruth. "There was always something going on, from practices and games to someone forgetting a jersey and Mom or Dad having to rush it to our games.

"I also remember how supportive our community was and how our moms would make us goodie bags for big games and district tournaments," she said. "Most of all, I remember having such a strong competitive drive and passion for volleyball from a young age. Volleyball was a huge part of our family and looking back, it's the little memories and all the support surrounding those seasons that mean the most."

Gracie, along with her sisters Hannah, Lilly and Violet have all played for the Medina/Pingree-Buchanan volleyball team. There has been at least one Bohl sister on the team since 2016. Violet, the youngest of the four, is in her senior season with the Thunder this year.

"I've been watching them play ever since I was 2 years old," Violet said. "They made me want to be just like them. Seeing them perform and be so good at volleyball and all the sports they played was an experience not many people get to see. Having three different sisters who all played in different ways and styles was something I really looked up to as a kid and a younger sister. I also have always admired, and what they've taught me is to not play for myself, but to as a setter, play to make your teammates succeed. My sister's faith in the Lord has also played a huge part in what's made me succeed and to give glory not to myself, but to God."

Violet began playing volleyball in elementary school. She has been on the high school team since her freshman year.

She is a fourth-year starter at the setter position. Last season, Violet was responsible for 1,147 assists and 514 digs. She made 61 kills and 12 blocks and delivered 36 aces from the service line.

"I am so proud of Violet and the setter she is," Hannah said. "I remember when Violet came to me when she was in elementary school, and she told me Jacie wanted her to be the setter and she didn't want that position. I told her I knew she was going to be good as a setter and to do her best and try it. Now look at her breaking records and making it to state with her team. I am beyond proud, and now I'm taking my toddler to her games."

All four Bohl sisters have set for the Medina/Pingree-Buchanan program.

"Not all of us wanted to be setters initially during our younger years, our coaches saw that we all fit best into the role of a setter," Lilly said. "It must run in the family."

In her career, Violet has notched 3,596 assists and 1,367 digs. She was named to the 2025 NDHSCA All-State Second Team last season. This year, Violet has made 510 assists, 213 digs and 67 kills.

"There were times that I would rather have been an outside hitter; at the end of the day, I trusted my coach and wherever she felt I fit best," Gracie said. "Every once in a while, my teammate, Megan Moser, would switch things up and set me during our rotation so I could get a hit in."

Gracie started playing volleyball in elementary school and continued all the way through her senior year of high school. She was on varsity beginning her eighth grade year and played at the varsity level throughout the rest of her high school career.

"My sisters motivated me in so many ways," Gracie said. "I wanted to set a good example for my younger sisters, not only through leadership on the court but also through my faith and the way I carried myself. They pushed me to work hard, give my best, and remember that if I left everything out on the court, I had done my part. Most importantly, they reminded me that all glory belongs to God and that no matter the outcome, I needed to trust in Him and His plan."

Hannah was the first of the sisters to set a new school record for assists made in a season.

"I remember my sisters either playing on the court with me or looking in the stands, always cheering me on," Hannah said. "In our house, someone always had a volleyball, bouncing it off walls or ceilings. Our dad actually taped a volleyball court in the basement for us to practice with."

Hannah started playing in sixth grade and started playing varsity her junior year of high school. Hannah and Gracie played together for one year, and Gracie and Lilly for two.

Lilly played volleyball from elementary school to high school. She was on the varsity team freshman year through her senior year.

"I've had numerous special memories with both my older sister Gracie and younger sister Violet," Lilly said. "Growing up in the sport, my sister Gracie was a role model for me, demonstrating hard work during her time as a setter, and eventually I was able to play with my younger sister Violet as she grew into the talented setter that she is today. During our time at practices and games, we not only grew as teammates but also closer as sisters."

Lilly and Violet played together for one season.

"(In our basement) I would pepper by myself on the walls; my parents were not a fan of that and would always beg my parents and sisters to pepper with me outside," Violet said. "... It took lots of begging, but when they agreed, I always made it my time to shine and to show them how much 'better' I was than them."

According to the stats, Violet has grown up to be the best out of the four.

"I didn't exactly get a choice to not be a setter," she said. "It's funny because when I found out I was going to be the JV setter, I cried, actually. But Jacie and my other coaches saw potential in me, and I am so grateful for that now."

In her four years on varsity, Violet made the All-State, Second-Team, accomplished over 1,000 sets in a single season, set a record for most assists in a game, which was set in the 2025 region championship game, and currently holds the school record for assists. She also has the most career assists out of her sisters.

"Although we all had a little friendly competition over the years and each of us ended up breaking the other's assist records at some point, ... Violet has the most impressive list of accolades for volleyball," Gracie said. "Violet also had the opportunity to take her team to the state tournament, which was really special. We were always pushing each other to be better."

The Thunder has played at the state tournament the past two years and is on track to make it this season. Currently, the Thunder is 20-6 overall, 11-1 in Division B, Region 1 play and 7-1 in Division B, Region 1, District 2. The Region 1 tournament is set to begin on Nov. 9 and will run through Nov. 12.

"It is so special thinking back to Violet coming to our games when she was just a toddler and watching her grow into the beautiful young woman she is today," Gracie said. "I remember playing pepper with her outside after practices, and now it feels like we blinked and she's already a senior. Time really does fly by.

"I would encourage Violet to soak up every moment, play with all her heart, but most importantly, give all the glory to God," she said. "Remember that he has gifted you with your abilities and talents, and use those gifts to honor him. Enjoy every second of these last few months, trust in His plan through every high and low, and don't let the outcome take away from the joy of the game or the opportunity God has given you."

Violet said she is thankful for her sisters' undying support through her career.

"I remember always going to my sister's games and being in awe of them playing, thinking I can't wait to play like that when I grow up," Violet said. "I remember having such a passion and love for it. ... My sisters are and always will be role models of mine on and off the court. The support they show me is something I can't compare anything to and am so grateful for them to be a part of this sport and something I know I can always look back on."
authors: Katie Ringer, The Jamestown Sun, N.D.

articles.title: West Region volleyball tournament coming to Jamestown
articles.summary: Nov. 11—JAMESTOWN — A lot of people are planning on coming to the Buffalo City this weekend. Jamestown High School is set to host the 2026 West Region volley...
articles.body:
Nov. 11—JAMESTOWN — A lot of people are planning on coming to the Buffalo City this weekend.

Jamestown High School is set to host the 2026 West Region volleyball tournament beginning on Nov. 12. The quarterfinal round is set to start with a 1 p.m. quarterfinal between top-seeded and 12-time defending region champion Bismarck Century and Williston. The second quarterfinal is a tilt between Mandan and Bismarck High. First serve for game No. 2 is scheduled for 3 p.m.

Jamestown will be featured in the third quarterfinal of the day. Sara Hegerle's crew is set to take on Minot at 5 p.m. Minot North and Bismarck Legacy are set to close out the day with a game that is set to begin at 7 p.m.

While Jamestown has never captured a West Region championship, the Blue Jays have reached the championship match 10 times as tournament runner-up — the last time coming in 2025. They enter looking to finally break through on their home floor.

Outside of Century, regional titles have been scarce across the field. Bismarck High last hoisted the West Region championship trophy in 2010 while Minot High earned the WDA championship in 2007. Williston was named the WDA champs in 2006 while Mandan captured back-to-back crowns in 2001 and 2002. The Blue Jays along with Legacy and second-year varsity program Minot North are all pursuing their first-ever West Region title.

articles.title: 2 Detroit Lions Will Almost Certainly Miss Germany Game
articles.summary: Dan Campbell provides updates on DJ Wonnum, Cade Mays, and D.J. Reed ahead of the Detroit Lions' Week 10 matchup against New England.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions received some encouraging injury news Wednesday as they prepare for Sunday's matchup against the New England Patriots in Germany. However, head coach Dan Campbell also revealed that two key starters remain unlikely to play.

According to Wednesday's update, Campbell said defensive end DJ Wonnum is expected to return to practice after missing Sunday's 19-9 victory over the Miami Dolphins with a concussion. As long as Wonnum avoids any setbacks, Campbell believes he should be available against New England.

Unfortunately, the news wasn't nearly as promising for center Cade Mays and cornerback D.J. Reed. Neither player is expected to practice Wednesday, and Campbell indicated that both are doubtful at best for Sunday's game.

Wonnum's potential return would provide an important boost to Detroit's defensive front. The veteran pass rusher was among five Lions ruled out against Miami , leaving Detroit shorthanded on defense.

According to the Lions' official November 6 injury report , Wonnum did not practice last week while dealing with his concussion. Wednesday's expected return represents an encouraging development, although his availability remains dependent on avoiding setbacks and receiving the necessary clearance.

Meanwhile, the outlook for Mays and Reed remains concerning. Both players were already expected to miss last Sunday's game , and neither appears particularly close to returning.

Mays continues to deal with an ankle injury, while Reed is recovering from a hip injury. According to the Lions' official inactive report against Miami , veteran Juice Scruggs started at center in Mays' absence, while Detroit relied on its secondary depth without Reed.

The Lions will continue monitoring all three players throughout the week before making final decisions on their availability. For now, Wonnum appears to be trending in the right direction, while Mays and Reed face an uphill battle to suit up against the Patriots.

articles.title: NFL Week 10 Fantasy Football OROY Stock Watch Rankings: Makai Lemon & KC Concepcion Climbs the Leaderboard
articles.summary: Some first-year stars are making serious noise, while others are watching their stock plummet as the fantasy football season heats up.
articles.body:
Fantasy football isn't for the faint of heart, and if you're still relying on preseason hype, you're already dead in the water. Welcome to the rookie stock watch, where a single explosive route can launch a waiver-wire darling into league-winning mortality, and one awkward tackle can turn your prized dynasty jewel into an expensive hospital roommate.

The injury bug has been eating well, workload trends are swinging wildly, and half the first-year class is either breaking out or breaking down. Let's slice through the noise, check the charts, and figure out which rookies are making the biggest fantasy impact through Week 10.

Concepcion is enjoying a massive surge in fantasy stock driven by electric, explosive production and a rapidly expanding target share. His ability to turn catches into chunk gains and his elusiveness in space have quickly made him the focal point of the offense and an absolute weapon in PPR formats. Fantasy managers who secured him early are now reaping the rewards as his consistent target volume elevates him from a volatile boom-or-bust option into a reliable weekly starter.

Coleman continues to climb up fantasy boards thanks to an increasingly heavy backfield workload and highly valuable receiving involvement. His physical running style establishes a high baseline of rushing volume, while his reliable hands out of the backfield makes him a trusted safety valve on third downs. This dual-threat usage elevates both his weekly floor and overall ceiling, giving fantasy managers a stable asset who can grind out tough yards and punish defenses in the passing game.

Lemon has surged into fantasy relevance on the back of strong recent production fueled by expanding snap counts and consistent trust from the coaching staff. His route-running precision and reliable hands allows him to exploit soft spots in zone coverage, turning late-round draft capital into immediate fantasy starter viability. As his chemistry with Joe Milton deepens, his target volume should stabilize to the point where managers can plug him into starting lineups with confidence.

Sadiq has seen his fantasy stock slide downward due to declining playing time and increasingly inconsistent target involvement. Early-season optimism has cooled as offensive shifts have limited his route participation and red-zone opportunities, leaving him stranded on the waiver wire in many shallower leagues. Until the offensive scheme adjusts to feature him more prominently or his snap share rebounds, he remains a speculative stash that is very difficult to trust in active starting lineups.

Love's ongoing availability concerns continue to suppress his current trade value. Although his raw talent is undisputed, missing crucial development time on the field makes it nearly impossible for fantasy managers to insert him into starting lineups with any degree of confidence. Managers holding him must exercise patience, treating him as a high-upside stash whose true dividends will likely be paid down the road once his health issues are fully behind him.

Tate's fantasy profile remains deeply volatile due to persistent availability and injury concerns that overshadow his impressive efficiency when healthy. Whenever he steps onto the field , his explosive traits and high-end metrics flash brilliantly, but unpredictable participation creates weekly headaches for managers trying to time his active weeks.

articles.title: Jaguars' Cam Little wins AFC Special Teams Player of the Week
articles.summary: Cam Little earned AFC Special Teams Player of the Week honors after Jacksonville's win against the Baltimore Ravens.
articles.body:
Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little was named the AFC Special Teams Player of the Week for his performance against the Baltimore Ravens . Little made all four of his field goal attempts while converting three extra point tries for a career-best 15 points in the win last week.

Little has made 14-of-16 field goal attempts while also converting 25 of his 26 extra point attempts this season. It's a consistency that's helped the Jaguars rise to the top of the AFC South with a 6-2 record through eight games.

Little's heroics against the Philadelphia Eagles saved the Jaguars from a defeat in London earlier this season as he netted a walk-off 57-yard field goal .

Jaguars battle Philadelphia Eagles in London. See the photos

The third-year kicker out of Arkansas owns the record for the longest made field goal in NFL history with a 68-yard make against the Las Vegas Raiders in 2025. He also made a 70-yard field goal during the 2025 preseason, boasting a leg strength that not many can replicate.

But it's his accuracy that's valued in Jacksonville as he's made 71-of-79 attempts in his career. This is the second time he's earned Player of the Week honors, winning the award in Week 9 after making the 68-yard field goal against the Raiders .

Little is the third player to win Player of the Week honors in the 2026 season, joining linebacker Foye Oluokun and safety Rayuan Lane .

articles.title: What Tyler Shough told rookie WR after critical fumble vs. Browns
articles.summary: Here's what New Orleans Saints Tyler Shough told rookie wide receiver Barion Brown after a critical fumble against the Cleveland Browns.
articles.body:
Here's a cool moment from Sunday's game between the New Orleans Saints and Cleveland Browns . All looked lost when rookie wide receiver Barion Brown fumbled on a punt return with four minutes left in the first half, having cut one way across the field before reversing course and trying to go the other direction. He just tried to do too much with the ball in his hands, and the play ended with Cleveland regaining possession at the New Orleans 19-yard line.

It would be easy for a young player to feel discouraged in that moment, or for a veteran to lay into him on the sideline. Instead, second-year quarterback Tyler Shough had words of reassurance.

"Hey, best part is you get to do it again. We get to go out there and play again. It's all good. They say, shoot your shot, get your yards, get down," Shough told Brown , in a video shared by the NFL. "We've all fumbled before, you know what I'm saying? You learn from it brother, it ain't going to happen again. Keep your energy, keep your juice, because we're gonna need you on another play. You know what I'm saying?"

Shough pointed to the scoreboard; the score was still tied, the two-minute warning was coming up, and the New Orleans defense got a stop, forcing the Browns into a turnover on downs at the goal line. It was time to go back to work.

"I mean, you can be mad about it later, but right now, how you talk to yourself matters. So, after the game, be (expletive) pissed. But right now, who cares? You know what I'm saying?" Shough added.

Shough had looked Brown's way just minutes earlier on a 52-yard reception, and the rookie finished with 198 all-purpose yards for his work on offense and special teams. He's in a position to make an impact each week. He just needs to make the most of those opportunities and, as Shough reminded him, stay present and focused. Let's see how he bounces back in Week 10 against the Carolina Panthers.
